anf_compare.notes: No PD English exists. Ps 148:3 follows LXX; Matt 6:7/6:12 and Ps 7:10 familiar wording.

choices.english: something up to even the sun
choices.term: ἔστι τι καὶ τοῦ ἡλίου ἐφ᾽ ἡμῖν
choices.why: The formula extends to heavenly bodies deliberately — the sunrise objection's answer turns on it.

choices.english: dancing in heaven savingly for the whole
choices.why: choreuo = dance in ordered chorus; the stars' harmony is choral, befitting Ps 148.

choices.english: with motion from their own cause

pass_a_gloss: Regarding prayer for sunrise: there is an 'up to us' even of the sun, praising God with the moon (Ps 148:3 sun/moon; stars/light). As God uses each earthly 'up to us' for earthly need, so the heavenly world's order runs by the sun/moon/stars' 'up to us' — untransgressing, firm, stable, wise. Praying concerning another's 'up to us' is not vain — much more concerning the stars' saving dance. Earthly impressions provoke our instability or better-inclining; but what impression could shift heavenly ones — reason-fitted souls, self-caused motion, purest aetherial bodies — from their world-beneficial course?
pass_b_english: And regarding prayer for the sun to rise, this must be said. There is something up to even the sun, with it praising God together with the moon — praise him, it says, sun and moon. And evidently the moon's too, and consequently all the stars': for praise him, it says, all stars and light.

As we said God uses each earthly one's 'up to us' for some earthly need, appointing them fittingly, so we must suppose he appointed the whole heavenly world and the stars' harmonious course and motion for the whole by the sun and moon and stars' 'up to us' — untransgressing(?) and firm and stable(?) and wise. And if I pray not in vain concerning another's 'up to us,' much more concerning the 'up to us' of the stars dancing in heaven savingly for the whole. Though one may say of earthly things that certain impressions arising from surroundings provoke our instability or our better-inclining to do or say this or that — but for the heavenly, what arising impression could dislodge and shift, from its world-beneficial course, each of those having such a soul fitted by reason, with motion from their own cause(?) and using such an aetherial, purest body (Psalm 148:3)?
